articleinfo.title: UBL Example Documents: Method and Rationale Version 1.0

abstract.para: This note describes how a coherent set of UBL example documents is created and maintained: a fictional world of organisations that exchange UBL documents with each other, and for every value in every example the reason why it fits the semantic meaning of its element in that context.

legalnotice.title: Notices
legalnotice.para: This is a proposal draft, prepared outside the OASIS UBL Technical Committee. It has not been contributed to, reviewed by or approved by the TC, and it is not an OASIS work product. It may be proposed to the TC as a contribution for a Committee Note.
The layout uses the OASIS DocBook publishing stylesheets (spec-0.9), as used by the OASIS UBL TC. UBL is an OASIS Standard and ISO/IEC 19845.

section.title: Purpose
section.para: UBL defines hundreds of document types and thousands of elements. Its definitions say what an element means, but readers also need to see how an element is used: with which value, in which context, and in relation to the other documents in a business process.

This note describes a method for creating UBL example documents that show exactly that. The examples form one coherent set: they share the same organisations, products and timeline, and documents that belong together refer to each other the way they would in real exchanges.

section.title: Scope
section.para: The method covers:

listitem.para: the fictional world in which the examples take place;
how a value is chosen for an element, and how the reason for that choice is recorded;
how examples are checked, within a document and across documents;
how examples are reviewed and maintained over UBL versions.

section.para: The examples illustrate UBL. They do not define a profile, a customization or a national implementation, and a value used in an example is never the only valid value.

section.title: Starting point
section.para: The example set starts from the sample documents that OASIS published with each UBL 2.x release. Their history, from UBL 2.0 to UBL 2.5, is kept in the repository, one document per commit.

section.title: One fictional UBL world
section.para: All examples take place in the same fictional world: a set of organisations that do all their business with UBL. Documents that belong together, such as a catalogue, an order, a despatch advice and an invoice, or the transport and customs documents for the same goods, tell one consistent story.

section.title: Universal, not tied to one region
section.para: The world includes business within one country, within a region and between continents. No country, legal system or process is the default. Where an example uses a country-specific identifier or rule, it is one illustration among others, not the way UBL has to be used.

section.title: Every value has a reason
section.para: For each element in each example, the reason for its value is recorded: why the value fits the semantic meaning of the element, as defined by UBL, in the context of that document and that business situation. The reason refers to the UBL definition first. Country rules or a specific process only appear as illustrations.

section.title: Proven, not only plausible
section.para: Values are checked automatically:

listitem.para: the document is valid against the UBL schemas and code lists;
the document is consistent in itself, for example totals, dates and internal references;
the documents are consistent with each other, for example parties, references between documents and quantities along a process.

section.title: Open and reproducible
The UBL example world
section.para: This section describes the world as decided on 18 November 2026. The examples are being brought into line with it, and until that work is done some of them still differ from what is written here; where they do, analysis/worklist.md and analysis/worklist-decisions.md say what is to be done.
All examples take place in one fictional world. It is built in layers. Each layer adds one kind of data, is kept in its own file, and is checked before the next layer builds on it.

row.entry: names, currencies, tax schemes, identifier and address schemes
the organisations: place on the map, role, identity
the flows of documents between the parties
what the parties sell: goods and services, with prices
extracted from the UBL 2.5 semantic model
the world's code lists, and which code element uses which
the transactions, national and community specifications and process profiles the documents claim
the first UBL 2 version of each element, from the published models of UBL 2.0 to 2.5

section.title: Countries
section.para: The world has three countries: Urvania, Bayvarra and Lisavu, whose initials spell UBL. Two share a land border on the mainland; the third is an island overseas. They differ on purpose, so that the examples show how UBL carries different national arrangements in the same structure:

listitem.para: Urvania (XU) has a value added tax in the style of the EU VAT: charged at every stage, deducted by businesses, not charged on exports.
Bayvarra (XB) is a federal country whose states levy a retail sales tax, charged once, on the sale to the final consumer. Sales for resale, exports and sales to public bodies are exempt.
Lisavu (XL) has no general sales tax. Customs collects an import consumption tax on every import when goods enter the island, and a customs duty on goods from outside the Trade Accord.

section.para: The tax schemes are identified with UN/EDIFACT 5153 codes: VAT, STT (state or provincial sales tax), CUD (customs duty) and IMP (import tax). Because 5153 has no code for a national sales tax, Bayvarra levies its sales tax at state level, which also gives the state in its addresses a purpose. Bayvarra has two states and a federal territory. Upland State lies inland, on the plateau in the west, with Marrowdale and the wheat land; Coastal State lies along the east coast, with Lumeport and Larkmouth. The Northern Territory, on the low north coast, is thinly populated: the fishing village of Gullhaven, where the gas plant stands, two fishing hamlets (Shinglebeck and Ploverness) and a few sheep stations, on land used only for grazing. The territory levies its own rate of the same sales tax: 4 %, against 5 % in Upland State and 6.5 % in Coastal State. Which state a place is in follows from its place on the map.

XU, XB and XL are ISO 3166-1 user-assigned codes, which exist for exactly this purpose; each follows the initial of its country's name. ISO 4217 has no such range for currencies. The world's currencies follow the ISO 4217 convention of the country code plus the initial of the currency's name: the ferra of Urvania (XUF), the lume of Bayvarra (XBL) and the coral of Lisavu (XLC). The convention limits the names: ISO 4217 already uses XUA and XBA to XBD, so Urvania's currency cannot start with an A and Bayvarra's not with A to D. Each code is checked against the current ISO 4217 list, so that none is a real code.

The three currencies also differ in their minor unit, because currencies do: the ferra has none (amounts are whole ferra, as with the Japanese yen), the lume has two decimals, and the coral three (as with the Bahraini or Kuwaiti dinar). An example that only ever shows two decimals hides a case that software must handle. Neither the countries nor the currencies are in the UBL default code lists. UBL lets trading partners use their own code lists in the second phase of validation, so the world has its own: copies of the UBL 2.5 default lists, unchanged, with the world's codes added and their own identification.

The land border between Urvania and Bayvarra has two parts. From the border crossing, where the largest river of the plateau joins the main river, it follows the main river down to the sea, and then the middle line of the estuary: all land south of the river is Urvania. North of the crossing it follows the watershed, so that Urvania keeps the whole valley of that plateau river. The boundary convention of about 1857 drew it so (see "History"). The sawmill stands in Marrowdale, in Upland State, and buys its logs from the Upland State Forest, a managed forest on the slope where the upland falls towards the town, about 50 km north of the river.

Each country also has an address format (address in world/countries.json), which fixes the lines of an address: first the optional lines (attention, department, in-house mail, post box, building, floor and room), then the street and number (street first in Urvania, number first in Bayvarra and on the island), additional street, block and plot, quarter, and last the town line (postal code before the town in Urvania; the town, state and postal code in Bayvarra), with the province in Urvania and the district and a description of the way on the island. The province is a subdivision of the country, like a Bayvarran state, so it is written in CountrySubentity; UBL's Region names an informal area or a group of countries, which no address of the world has. Where a delivery goes to a gate or a dock, that is a delivery location with its own identifier, not part of the postal address. A field the address does not have is left out with its line. A name in two languages is written on its line in both, the national language first, then /, then English, and the number once: <Urvanian street> / <English street> 12 in Urvania, 35 <Lisavan street> / <English street> on the island. Every address that has a street, a building number or a post box carries the code of its country's format in AddressFormatCode, and where a party writes its address in AddressLine elements, one function makes the lines from the structured fields, so they cannot disagree. The build checks all three. A farm on the island has no house number: its track is described instead ("at kilometre 4").

Urvania's energy market is unbundled, as the EU's is: a gas-fired power station produces electricity, a grid operator runs the electricity and gas networks and reads the meters, and a retail company buys the energy and bills the customers. The gas comes from an offshore field off Bayvarra's north coast and crosses the border by pipeline. The Trade Accord's energy protocol of 2007 asks for less than that: a network is run with its own accounts and its own management and is open to others on equal terms; whether it becomes a company of its own is each country's choice, and an isolated system is exempt. Urvania chose the full split in 2007. Bayvarra keeps one energy company with a separately run network division, and the island, connected to no one, has one company that does everything, so the three countries show three arrangements. The gas is measured at a border metering station on Bayvarra's side. The producer declares each month's export in one declaration, with a consignment for each buyer (the power station and the retail company), and each buyer declares its own import. Montebrio Power is one of Urvania's power stations, a gas-fired station of about 40 MW; the retail company also buys electricity from the others.

The supply of electricity, gas, water and telephone to end customers is a national matter under the Accord: each country keeps its own utilities, public or under national licence, and no utility of one country supplies end customers in another. Ferrano Energy serves Urvania, the Coastal State Water Company Bayvarra's Coastal State, and Selanu Telecom the island. What crosses the border is wholesale energy: the energy protocol opened the trade in gas and electricity between producers, networks and suppliers, and since 2011 Kelpstone Gas of Bayvarra sells gas by pipeline to Urvania's power station and to Ferrano Energy. Because the customers of a protected supplier cannot go elsewhere, the three countries agreed minimum rules for utility bills; one of them is the period to pay (see "Money and payment").

section.title: History
section.para: Before the Europeans came, the Urvanians farmed the wet valley of the main river and the hills to the west of it. Their town, Ruldraz, grew where the valleys meet and where the river stops being navigable, below the rapids. It is the town the Italians later called Ferrano, and its old town still carries the Urvanian name.

The first Europeans to reach it came from Tuscany. In reality, Grand Duke Ferdinando I of Tuscany sent the Thornton expedition from Livorno to Guiana and the Amazon in 1608–09, the only official attempt of an Italian state before unification at a colony overseas; a second voyage, with settlers from Livorno and Lucca, was cancelled when the Grand Duke died in 1609. In the world that second voyage sailed, in 1609–10, and reached Ruldraz. This is invented. A small Tuscan trading post lasted some decades and faded in the 18th century. It left Ferrano's quarter Borgo Toscano and the chapel of San Ranieri del Guado, by an old ford of the upper river.

In the 1820s British settlers landed at Larkmouth, at the mouth of the largest river of the east coast: a sheltered harbour, with fresh water and dry grassland behind it. They spread over the dry east and the plateau as graziers and wheat farmers. Larkmouth was their first town and first capital, and Bayvarra keeps the landing as Settlers' Day. The settlers held the coast through their own company, without the Crown: Britain's Colonial Office avoided new colonies in those years for what they cost. In the late 1830s the company kept a small trading station at the narrows of the estuary, on the shore of the bay, where a brook gave fresh water; the narrows command the entry to the river.

About 1840 the Sardinian corvette Euridice came from Sardinia's naval station on the Río de la Plata. Because the station was the company's and the Crown had no sovereignty over the river, the warship of a friendly kingdom could sail past the station up the river to Ruldraz. The Urvanian rulers signed a treaty of protection with Sardinia, which revived the old Tuscan claim, and Forte Euridice was built about 1842 in the angle of the main river and the largest river of the plateau. The station on the Plata and the corvette are real: Sardinia kept a naval station and a consulate general there from 1837, with some ten thousand subjects, most of them Ligurians, and the Euridice was stationed there in 1836–38 before it sailed up the Amazon. Its voyage to the world is invented; Italy's first real possession was Assab on the Red Sea, bought by the Rubattino shipping company in 1869 and taken over by the state in 1882. Ligurian fishermen from the Plata settled under the protectorate at Marina Ligure on the south coast.

The treaty made Britain act. It annexed the coast and the dry east, as cheaply as it could, fortified the station at the narrows and laid out the town of Lumeport there, about 1841, as the colony's seat; as the river trade grew it became the capital in Larkmouth's place. Britain did not take the valley: Sardinia protected it, it was densely peopled and would have been costly to conquer, and the settlers wanted the grazing land, not the valley. A real parallel is New Zealand, which Britain annexed in 1840 only under pressure, among it the fear of a French settlement at Akaroa, and where it then let the French settlers keep their settlement. Sardinia fought beside Britain and France in the Crimean War (1855) and sat at the Congress of Paris (1856). A boundary convention of about 1857 then set the border along the main river below the confluence and along the watershed north of it, with free navigation of the river to the sea, the principle the Final Act of the Congress of Vienna laid down for international rivers in 1815 and the Berlin Act extended in 1885. The crossing has been known by the fort ever since. In 1861 the Kingdom of Italy inherited the protectorate, and Urvania stayed an Italian territory until 1941.

In the late 19th century Bayvarra built its railway, and villages grew at its stations. On Lisavu, English settlers laid out cotton estates in the 19th century on the dry north-eastern plain, at Lintwell and Bollworth, and named the island's capital Port Wrenfield. In 1941, in the Second World War, British forces took Urvania and put it under British administration, which stayed after Italy renounced its colonies in the peace treaty of 1947. (In the real treaty, article 23 renounces Italy's possessions in Africa; in the world the renunciation also covers Urvania.) The British kept the Italian place and street names, and Urvania kept a continental cast in its institutions, among them its value added tax and its Italian-style bank codes. It became independent in 1962, bilingual in Urvanian and English, and built a protected economy around state mining, state energy and its own manufacturers: Ferrano Energy dates from 1949, Serravona Mining from 1958, and Valdara Industries, the bench maker, was founded in the year of independence. Bayvarra's settler economy is older than Urvania's state; the Bank of Lumeport was founded in 1903. The exact dates of the first landing, the treaty and the boundary convention are not yet settled, and neither is when the island was first settled or how Bayvarra and the island became independent.

In 1974 Bayvarra and Lisavu signed the Lumeport Agreement. The island's cotton entered Bayvarra free of duty, a regular shipping service linked the two, and the island's coral was tied to the lume. The island kept its duties on imports. Tidewell Ocean Lines was founded that year to run the service, and the agreement called other companies into being: the Port of Selanu was formed as a company ahead of it, a customs broker on the island followed in 1975, and in 1976 a Bayvarran forwarder and the Lumeport Textile Mill, built to spin the island's duty-free cotton.

Urvania opened its economy in the early 1990s, as several real countries did in those years. In 1994 it joined the two others in the Lumeport Trade Accord, signed in Lumeport, which turned the agreement of 1974 into a free trade area of all three countries; the Accord takes its name from it. The Accord entered into force on 1 January 1996. The ferra joined the lume and the coral at a fixed parity. The island stopped charging duty on its partners' goods and kept its import consumption tax, which falls on every import whatever its origin, food included, which the island taxes to encourage its own farms: it is the island's substitute for a sales tax, and the reason it could afford to join. Lumeway Distribution became Valdara's distributor for Bayvarra and the island in that year, under a distribution agreement, which is why Valdara's benches reach the island through Lumeport. Hauliers, forwarders, customs brokers, a factoring company, a border terminal and Urvania's numbering agency were set up around that time to serve the new cross-border trade.

Later protocols of the Accord followed. The energy protocol of 2007 opened the wholesale trade in gas and electricity and asked for networks to be run apart from supply, while the supply to end customers stayed national; Urvania's Ferrano Grid was split off that year. In 2011 Kelpstone Gas began producing from its offshore field and the pipeline brought gas to Urvania; Ferrano Energy and Ferrano Grid, electricity companies until then, took up gas as a second business. Further protocols gave the three countries common procurement rules, the payment link and card schemes, and electronic business documents, which is why they share these and the code lists although each keeps its own taxes; their dates are not yet settled. The Accord also keeps public services national: it leaves the supply of electricity, gas, water and telephone to end customers to each country and sets a common minimum for the customers of those utilities.

The companies' founding years follow this history: the old trades before 1962 (the river barges, marine insurance, the island's cotton ginnery, the water company); the companies the agreement of 1974 called for; and the Accord's wave from 1996 to 1999 (the haulier, the factoring company, the border terminal, Valdara's logistics arm, the numbering agency, island warehousing). Each party has its own founding date, headcount and turnover, from which its size class follows. The table of founding years and figures in analysis/worklist-decisions.md is a current base, open to correction; each party's day and month of founding are in world/parties.json.

section.title: Geography
section.para: The mainland is a land of about 550 by 411 km and about 159,000 km² in the middle of the South Atlantic, astride the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, far from every continent. Urvania holds the west and all the land south of the main river, about 90,500 km², about the size of Portugal; Bayvarra most of the plateau, the dry east and the north coast, about 70,100 km². Lumeport stands on the east coast, on a bay at the mouth of the estuary. Lisavu is an isolated volcanic island about 1,080 km east of Lumeport, about 116 by 85 km and 7,100 km², smaller than Cyprus, standing on a seamount of the Walvis Ridge.

The position is a current base: the mainland centred on 30.0° South, 15.0° West, from about 28.2° to 31.8° South and from 17.9° to 12.0° West (Ferrano at about 30.7° South, 15.5° West; Lumeport at about 31.0° South, 13.3° West), and the island around 33.0° South, 2.65° West, with Selanu at about 2.2° West (geography in world/countries.json). Both lie on the high seas, outside every country's waters and claims; the nearest real land is Tristan da Cunha, about 600 km south of the mainland's south coast. It is still to be confirmed against a nautical chart that both areas lie outside the 200-nautical-mile zones of the nearest islands and that no extended-shelf claim or sea-bed licence reaches them. The mainland lies at the latitude of southern Brazil and South Africa, and the island, at 33° South, is warm enough for cotton.

The land is made from its geology (tools/terrain.py makes world/terrain.json from world/terrain-inputs.json): a volcanic massif in Urvania's north-west, which reaches about 1,920 m, and a rift valley 15 to 18 km wide, where the Mid-Atlantic Ridge runs under the land. The main river rises on the massif at about 1,510 m and runs 470 km through the rift valley to the sea. It is the trunk of one large basin of about 53,000 km², a third of the mainland, and the larger branch at every confluence; its tributaries come from the massif, the plateau and the southern hills. Just above Ferrano it falls through rapids, from about 124 to 91 m in about 12 km, which end navigation: the barges work below them. From the border crossing the river forms the border, and some 45 km above Lumeport it becomes a drowned estuary, which narrows at Lumeport before it opens into the bay. Urvania's western hills and the land south of the river are green and hilly, wet from the westerly winds; east of them the plateau of Upland State falls to the dry east of Coastal State, grazing and wheat land, and the north coast is low.

From the mainland the first sight of the island is its west coast: cliffs of about 115 to 435 m, with two bays where the land has slid into the sea, stacks and islets, and flats of landslide debris at their foot. That side faces the prevailing westerly wind and the ocean swell and has no port. The island is an eroded volcano, which rises to about 1,810 m some 25 km inland from the west coast and falls to the east. Ships round a cape to the lee side, where the port and the town of Selanu lie on a sheltered bay of the east coast, the airport on the plain about 10 km to the north, and the cotton on a plain of about 690 km² in the dry north-east, in the island's rain shadow: the high ground on the windward side catches the rain, and the lee side is drier and sunnier. An island cut off like this has to work for its ties, which is the story of the Lumeport Agreement and of the shipping line founded to serve it.
The countries have about 2.1 million people: Urvania about 1.2 million, Bayvarra about 800,000 and Lisavu about 60,000. Each capital holds about half its country's people. The towns:

row.entry: the capital; works, rail hub, river port below the rapids
the capital and the port city, at the estuary's narrows
the first landing and first capital; a wool and meat port at the mouth of the east river
inland town: distributor, sawmill, furniture maker, works
the island's capital and only town
villages: the mining village, the fishing village by the gas plant

section.para: Urvania also has seven country towns of 14,000 to 28,000 people, among them Portaggio at the head of the rapids, Fierabruna, the old cattle fair where two plateau rivers meet, Lanternino on a bay of the south coast, and Forte Euridice by the border. Bayvarra has ten railway and coast towns of 5,000 to 12,000, such as Tallowford, a ford market on a plateau river, and Brackenmere and Saltmere, which gave their names to Marrowdale firms. Lisavu's villages have at most 2,500 people each. Besides them there are about 430 villages and hamlets in Urvania, 160 in Bayvarra and 17 on the island, and scattered farms. Each lies where it has a reason to be (a ford or bridge, a confluence, a spring, a harbour, a crossroads, a mine), and its farmland follows the soil, the slope and the rain, not a ring round the village. Each town has quarters by period: in Ferrano the Urvanian old town, Borgo Toscano, the Italian quarters, the British-era suburb and the growth since independence; in Lumeport the settlers' Old Town, Government Hill and the docks of the colonial years and the suburbs after them.

Roads, railways and pipelines are laid over the land as a builder would lay them: main roads climb at most 7 %, minor roads 10 % and railways 2 %, and they follow the contours and cross few rivers. The largest bridges are Ferrano's road bridge, about 106 m above the river, the ore line's river bridge, 78 m high, and a viaduct over a side valley; no tunnel was worth its cost. The railways are the ore line from the mine down to Valdara's works at Ferrano, the line from Ferrano across the border to Lumeway's siding at Marrowdale, a line to the Port of Lumeport, and the wool line from Marrowdale down to Larkmouth's harbour. No main road runs south of the main river: the farmland there is served by minor roads, which reach the rest of the country over Ferrano's bridge.

Urvania separated its rail infrastructure from its train operators, as it separated its electricity grid from supply. A public body, the Rail Infrastructure Agency of Urvania, owns and maintains the tracks, allocates the train paths and runs the traffic control that dispatches every train, up to the border station; Ferrano Rail Cargo runs its trains on the paths it is given, and the intermodal hub at Ferrano only loads and unloads them. The European Union went part of that way: Directive 91/440/EEC required separate accounts and left the organisational separation optional, and an infrastructure manager must be a legally distinct body only since Directive 2012/34/EU as amended by Directive (EU) 2016/2370; full separation, as in Urvania, is one model a state may choose. Carriage by rail between the Accord's members follows the Accord's uniform rules for international carriage by rail, modelled on the CIM (COTIF Appendix B). Like the CIM they also cover a carriage by road within one member state that supplements the rail carriage under the same contract, so the rail carrier's haulage of a container to the hub is a stage of the rail contract.
Some places of the examples:

listitem.para: The mine. Serravona Mining works an underground mine on the massif's lower flank: an adit in the hillside at about 720 m, 29 km from Serravona, with its address in the village of Fucinalta, a small crushing and screening plant and a spoil heap; the hillside around it stays green. The ore line is laid up to the portal, where the wagons are loaded and weighed at Fucinalta mine siding.

The forest. The Upland State Forest, about 345 km² of compartments planted and felled by age, lies on the slope north of Marrowdale, between about 300 and 550 m, and supplies the sawmill in Marrowdale.
Lumeport's brook rises in the low hills west of the centre and runs through the town to the bay; it gave the town its first fresh water.

The river quay. Rinova Recovery stands on the river at Ferrano with a quay of its own, where the barge loads. The barge sails below the rapids, about 250 km down the river and the estuary to Lumeport, without locks.

The crossing. The road crosses the border at Valico Euridice (Menbaz) on the Urvanian side and Euridice Crossing on the Bayvarran side, with their customs posts facing each other, named after Forte Euridice, 8 km down the road.
The gas. The offshore platform stands about 80 km out from the gas plant at Gullhaven.

section.para: One square of the map is 3.5 km. The map is leading: a distance is the length of the route laid on the map, and every distance and time a document states comes from it, as listed in the place list (analysis/place-list.md, made by tools/place_list.py). By road Ferrano to Marrowdale is about 192 km and Marrowdale to Lumeport about 81 km; the ore line runs about 166 km; the gas pipeline runs about 207 km from the gas plant to the power station, its branch to the grid's city gate about 97 km, and the subsea line from the platform about 83 km. A document states the kilometres driven on its own leg, from party to party. Lumeport to Selanu is about 1,080 km in a straight line. By sea, out through the estuary and the bay and round the island's south-eastern cape, it is about 1,200 km, which the ship sails in about 48 hours at 13.5 knots. The island airline's freighter flies about 1,080 km between the airports, about 2½ hours from gate to gate in still air; its timetable allows 2 h 45 eastbound and 3 h 00 westbound, a margin for delays.

The printed map is an A3 landscape sheet at 1 : 2,500,000, with clear sea around the mainland. Lisavu stands beside it in a panel of its own, at the same scale: two panels in one frame, with a gutter between them and each with its own header and border, and a note that the island lies about 1,100 km east of Lumeport. The island is drawn nearer than it lies; the coordinates in the documents are its true position.

section.title: Languages
section.para: The countries speak differently. Bayvarra speaks English, the working language between the three countries. Urvania was an Italian territory and then under British rule; the British kept the Italian place and street names, while the people kept their own Urvanian names for the same places. Independent since 1962, Urvania is bilingual, Urvanian and English, and the inherited Italian names count as English: Ferrano is also Ruldraz, the older name of the Urvanians' town, and an address gives both, as in Brussels. The country towns have Italian and Urvanian names alike: Portaggio is Trenzir, Fierabruna Hihek and Forte Euridice Girkul. At the border crossing the Urvanian side is Valico Euridice, in Urvanian Menbaz, and the Bayvarran side Euridice Crossing. Bayvarra's places carry the English names its settlers gave them (Larkmouth, Marrowdale, Tallowford). The island is officially bilingual, as many Pacific islands are, in Lisavan and English, Lisavan having a Polynesian sound like the island's names. Both languages are invented, and their codes come from the range ISO 639 reserves for local use, qaa to qtz: qau for Urvanian and qal for Lisavan. A document between the countries, whose sender and receiver are in different countries, is in English, the working language of the Trade Accord. A sender from Urvania or the island gives the notes of its domestic documents in its own language and in English, each with its languageID, and those across a border in English only. A seller there names and describes its items in both (its name, description, warranty and what comes with it); a seller in Bayvarra does so in English only. Both countries name their streets and towns in both official languages, as Brussels and Canada do: UBL 2.5 lets an address repeat its street, city and state names, one per language. The island's capital keeps its Lisavan name as the primary one, and has the English name its English-speaking settlers gave it: Selanu is also Port Wrenfield, a name checked not to be a real place. Most of the island's villages have Lisavan names only (Felulaka, Natahoma, Setahu); the villages of the 19th-century cotton estates have English names with Lisavan ones beside them: Lintwell (Kefalasa) and Bollworth (Pakesa). The texts in the invented languages are made word by word from a fixed vocabulary, the English text being the reference. Real Polynesian languages are deliberately not used, and the invented words are checked against common words of real languages.

English is not one language across the three countries. Each country's English was shaped by its history and by the language spoken there before, and has drifted from standard English. Urvanian English carries the Italian place and street names the British kept, and stands beside Urvanian; Bayvarran English is the settlers' English and the working language between the three countries; Lisavan English stands beside Lisavan on the island and uses the Lisavan names for places. The three varieties are written en-XU, en-XB and en-XL. A party states the language of the exchange. In English it says which English it writes, in LocaleCode, from the world's list of locales, while Language/ID stays the plain language en. Only English has a locale, because it is the one language used in all three countries; Urvanian and Lisavan are each used in one country, and their plain codes say all. So an Urvanian company states qau at home and en with en-XU in a document to Bayvarra or the island.

A text keeps the English it was written in when it travels. A party's address, legal form and other master data are written by that party or its country's register and carry that party's variety in every document: a Bayvarran clerk copies an Urvanian address as it stands in Urvania's address register and does not translate it, so one address reads the same in every document of the world. Free text written for a document, such as a note or a description, carries the issuer's variety. One document can therefore hold two Englishes side by side: the buyer's note in Bayvarran English and the seller's address in Urvanian English. Whether and by whom an item's name and description are localised for the market it is sold in is not yet settled.

Port Wrenfield is still the official English name of the island's capital and stands in every address, the Lisavan name first, but it is fading from use: in speech and in writing, also in English, the town is Selanu, whoever writes. Proper names such as the port's and the bank's keep "Selanu", and the name lives on in the port quarter, Port Wrenfield. Using the Lisavan names for places is a trait of Lisavan English, as the Italian names are of Urvanian English. Urvania works the other way round: English text uses the inherited Italian name (Ferrano, Serravona) and Urvanian text the Urvanian one (Ruldraz, Drinzul).

section.title: Code lists
section.para: Every code in the examples comes from a code list, and every code element names its list in listID. The lists are made from one source, world/codelists/lists.json, as genericode files, together with the world's context/value associations, which say which list each element uses. Where a standard has a list for a concept, the world uses it; otherwise the Lumeport Trade Accord, the treaty between the three countries, has a regional list. A few lists are national, because the countries differ: legal forms, tax exemption reasons, Bayvarra's states and Urvania's customs tariff.

listitem.para: Lists of standards are used where UBL uses them (its default lists), where practice uses them (EN 16931 uses UN/EDIFACT 1001, 5189 and 7161), or where a standard is the authority for its domain: the IMO for emergency schedules and security levels, the WCO for the Harmonized System, the UN for product classification (CPC) and dangerous goods, ISO 20022 for payments, EPSG for coordinates, PRONOM for file formats, UN/ECE Recommendation 28 for means of transport and, as it refers air transport there, IATA's aircraft type codes. UBL is not "EDIFACT in XML", so a UN/EDIFACT list is not used just because it exists. Each is a world copy of the codes the world uses, with others of the same list, made from the copy of the source kept in world/codelists/sources; its listID is in UBL's text style, such as UN/EDIFACT EDED 1001 or WCO HS 2022. No code of such a list is invented.

Regional and national lists have short upper-case codes and a name in English, Urvanian and Lisavan; their listID is a URN such as urn:ubl-examples:world:codelist:AddressTypeCode or urn:ubl-examples:world:XB:codelist:CountrySubentityCode.

One list per concept. Elements that only qualify one concept share its list, as PreviousMeterReadingMethodCode and LatestMeterReadingMethodCode do. An element used for several things, such as TypeCode, gets one list per meaning, chosen by its parent element.
No filler. A code says something the receiver needs. Where "none" matters, it is a defined code, such as UN/EDIFACT 8339 code 4 "Not assigned" for goods without a packing group.

section.para: Some choices differ from common practice, on purpose:

listitem.para: Allowances and charges. An allowance takes its reason from UN/EDIFACT 5189 and a charge from 7161, as in EN 16931. Where 7161 has no code, the world uses 5189 for a charge too, with that list's listID (96 insurance, 48 interest on arrears), which EN 16931 does not allow. UBL's own default list for this element is labelled 5189 but holds the codes of UN/EDIFACT 4465, so the world replaces it.

Languages. Language codes are written in lower case, as ISO 639 and BCP 47 recommend; UBL's copy of the list is in upper case and merges the two alpha-3 codes of a language into one value. The world's list follows the ISO 639-2 registration authority and adds qau and qal. An English text is tagged with the English it was written in, en-XU, en-XB or en-XL, which BCP 47 allows for private use: a party's master data with that party's country, free text with the issuer's (see "Languages").
Invoice periods. InvoicePeriod/DescriptionCode describes the period (a month), as UBL defines it, not the tax point date code that EN 16931 puts there.

Document distribution. DocumentDistribution/DocumentTypeCode gives the type of the distributed document (a bill of lading), and DistributionTypeCode how the party receives it, original or copy: an original by courier, a scanned copy, the electronic document itself. UBL 2.5 deprecated the elements that said this before (CopyIndicator, MaximumCopiesNumeric, MaximumOriginalsNumeric, PrintQualifier), and an original is not a type of document.

Self-billing. Where the customer bills itself, as the cotton gin does for the farms' seed cotton, the world uses UBL's own SelfBilledInvoice and SelfBilledCreditNote, never an Invoice with type code 389 as EN 16931 and Peppol BIS do (their syntax binding has only Invoice and CreditNote). UBL 2.5 defines Invoice as "A document used to request payment" and SelfBilledInvoice as "An Invoice document created by the Customer (rather than the Supplier) in a Self Billing relationship"; its semantic definitions (§4.7) are what a document must conform to (§7.2). The type codes are UN/EDIFACT 1001 389 and 261: they repeat the root element, but their definitions are exact ("An invoice the invoicee is producing instead of the seller"), while 380 is a document "claiming payment". The gin's advance to a farm before the harvest is a self-billed prepayment invoice, type 386, which the final self-billed invoice deducts as its prepaid amount.
Procurement. The Accord's procurement rules are modelled on the EU's, without being EU law: its lists give the matching eForms or ESPD code.

Customs. The Accord is a free trade area, not a customs union: it has one customs data model with common procedures and statuses, while tariffs and the valuation of imports stay national. A procedure code is the requested procedure followed by the previous one, numbered differently from the EU's, so release for free circulation is 1000.

section.title: Identifiers
section.para: An identifier that comes from a scheme names it in schemeID; one that only its sender assigns, such as a document number or a line number, does not. The world's own schemes have lowercase URNs, as its first ones had (urn:ubl-examples:world:XB:register, urn:ubl-examples:world:endpoint), and a country's scheme carries its code (urn:ubl-examples:world:XU:tax, urn:ubl-examples:world:XB:vehicle-register). Real schemes keep the name their standard gives them, in the text style of UBL's listIDs: ISO 11649 for the creditor references, ISO 6166 for the securities, ISO6346 for the containers. Each scheme has its format in world/countries.json, with its check digit where it has one, and the build checks every identifier against it, as it checks the telephone numbers. A schemeID has no fixed format; the examples show two.

Every register issues its own numbers. A company's business register number, its tax number, its Codana number or GS1 company prefix and its other numbers are each issued by a different body, in that body's own series, and none is derived from another. Each scheme has a shape of its own, so that a value shows which scheme it belongs to, and no value of one scheme repeats the digits of a value of another. There are two stated exceptions. An electronic address is always an identifier the party already has, under a scheme code, never a new number: the network addresses a company by its business register number, as Peppol addresses a company by a number it already has. And customs registers a trader under its business register number, as the EU's EORI number is built from a national number. The build checks that no identifier of a party repeats the digits of another, apart from these two. An identifier is opaque: what a thing is and who issued its number is said by the elements around it, not read from the number.

Companies are entered in their country's register of businesses, and a document shows that entry: the register, its type, the company's status and its size class. Public bodies are not: customs services, chambers of commerce, the Trade Accord Council, the review board, the public works department, Codana and the other agencies are set up by law, so they carry no commercial register entry, no liquidation status and no size class. The ports and the island's telecom operator are companies owned by the state and are in the register like any company. A farmer on the island is entered in Lisavu's farm register, which renews a grower's registration each season.
Instead, each country keeps a register of its public bodies, on the model of Italy's IPA code, and the register gives each body a number of its own shape, derived from no other register:

row.entry: Index of Public Administrations of Urvania
xu_ and four lower-case letters or digits (xu_k4r7, the customs administration)
Federal list of public bodies of Bayvarra
ten digits, the first not 0 (3071845926, the customs and border service)
Government list of public bodies of Lisavu
GOV- and three digits (GOV-118, the customs service)
the Department of Agriculture of Lisavu (GOV-206), whose Plant Protection Service also issues the island's phytosanitary certificates
LFR- and four digits (LFR-0412, the cotton farm)

section.para: The Trade Accord Council, an international body seated in Lumeport, is in Bayvarra's federal list under its seat agreement with Bayvarra, so that it can deal with Bayvarran bodies, banks and the exchange network.

A public body's party identifier and the CompanyID of its legal entity carry that number under its register's scheme (urn:ubl-examples:world: and the scheme), and its electronic address is built from it, as a company's is from its business register number; the farm's likewise from its number in the farm register. Bayvarra's customs build a trader number from the last six digits of the trader's number in its register: a company's business register number, a public body's number in the federal list (XB-TR-397184 for the Lumeport Public Works Department). No real code of Italy's index starts with xu_. The build checks that each public body carries a number of its country's register in that register's shape, that no company carries a number in a public body's shape and no public body one in a company register's, and that the number repeats the digits of none of the party's other identifiers.

A code held in an identifier element, such as the tax category in TaxCategory/ID, the language in Language/ID, the hazard class or the Incoterms rule in DeliveryTerms/ID, names its code list in schemeID, with the list's listID (UN/EDIFACT EDED 5305, ISO 639), and the world's code list validation checks it like any code. What a dimension or a temperature is (AttributeID) is a code too, from three lists of the Trade Accord: one for dimensions (LENGTH, SEATHEIGHT …), each mapped to the UN/EDIFACT 6313 measured attribute in its description, one for temperatures (STORAGE, PRODUCT, AMBIENT …) and one for the rest (COLOUR, PALLETPLACES, TEU …).

Vehicles are registered nationally: plates, aircraft and railway wagons each have a national scheme. A wagon number follows the UIC's twelve digits with its check digit. Driving licences and identity numbers carry no schemeID: the element already says what they are, and the person's country says whose. Values that would look like real ones are made visibly fictional in the right format: the call signs and aircraft nationality marks use the series QU, QB and QL, which the ITU has not allocated, the ships' MMSIs the unallocated maritime identification digits 297, 298 and 299, and the wagons the UIC country codes 46, 47 and 48, which no railway uses. A container owner code is one the container register of the Bureau International des Containers does not hold, looked up on its public site.

Certificates and licences name their issuer in one of two ways. A number from a national register, such as Urvania's haulage licences and waste permits, Bayvarra's forestry register or its customs' register of bonded warehouses, names the register in schemeID, and with it the authority that keeps it, so no issuer party is needed. A certificate whose number is unique only with its issuer, such as an environmental, medical or sanitation certificate or the X.509 certificate of an access point, has no schemeID and names its issuer in IssuerParty. Rinova's granulate, for example, is certified for its recycled content by Certovira Certification, an accredited certification body in Ferrano that audits the plant every year under a recycled-content scheme following EN 15343:2007, as industry schemes such as RecyClass do; the certificate travels in the product information Rinova sends its buyer, not in the order, the invoice or the customs declaration.

Payment cards follow ISO/IEC 7812 in a range real cards cannot use: the major industry identifier 9, which is for national use, followed by the numeric code of the issuer's country (901, 902 and 903 are user-assigned in ISO 3166), the issuer's digits and a Luhn check digit. A chip application starts with its card scheme's application provider identifier from the national category D of ISO/IEC 7816-5 with the same country code. The Accord has three card schemes: Lumecard, the Bayvarran banks' domestic debit card, Coralcard on the island, and Tressa, an international credit card of the banks of all three countries; the names were checked against the real card networks. A till receipt shows the card number as the merchant's till prints it, never more than the first six and the last four digits, and never the card's security code or its dates. The department store's tills print only the last four digits; the trading company's shop on the island prints the first six and the last four. A webshop order is different: the card is not at hand, so the order carries the full number, the card's dates and its security code, and the store has the payment authorised before it reserves the goods. PCI DSS allows a merchant to hold the security code until the authorisation, never after.

section.title: Two identification systems
section.para: Each party identifies what it makes, ships and runs in one convention, as real companies do, chosen by whom it trades with.

GS1 is the system of Bayvarra's retail and distribution chain: the distributor Lumeway Distribution, the department store Brightmarket Stores, the furniture maker Brackenmere Furniture and the textile mill, which makes the shirts the store sells. They use a GTIN for their items, a GLN for themselves and their places (the distribution centre's rail siding, the store's goods-in), an SSCC for every pallet or skid they make up, and a GRAI for the distributor's own returnable pallets, which go back to it after each delivery to the store. Their company prefixes start with 952, which GS1 reserves for demonstrations and examples. The prefixes are licensed by GS1 Bayvarra, a not-for-profit association owned by its member companies. It began around 1981 as an article numbering association, when Brightmarket and other retailers wanted bar codes at the till, and took its present name in 2005, when the worldwide organisation became GS1. It gives a company a seven-digit company prefix, from which the company builds its own GTINs, GLNs, SSCCs and GRAIs. It also serves Lisavu, which has no such organisation of its own. It belongs to the story, not to the documents: no document names it until one has a reason to.

Codana, the Codana Identification Agency, is Urvania's public numbering body, founded in 1999 when the country opened its trade. It is an issuing agency under ISO/IEC 15459 with the issuing agency code KXU (K is the range for national public administrations, and XU is a user-assigned country code, so no real agency can hold it), and it keeps the organisation register behind the ISO/IEC 6523 code designator 0990, which no real scheme has. The bench maker, its warehouse, the mine, the recycler, the packaging maker, the gas producer, the power station and the grid operator work this way. Codana registers any company that asks, foreign ones too: Rivermouth Packaging and Kelpstone Gas are Bayvarran, but their customers are Valdara and the power station, so they use their customers' system. Codana gives each company a five-digit number, in order of registration since 1999, unrelated to the company's business register number; a large early member has a low one:

row.entry: a public body, set up by the state

section.para: A company registers once with Codana, and its one number serves as its party identifier (0990: and the number) and as the root of everything it labels (KXU and the number). This is how the real systems work: a D&B DUNS number is ISO/IEC 6523 code 0060 and issuing agency code UN, an Odette number 0177 and OD, and GS1 itself is 0088 (the GLN) and the agency codes 0 to 9. Codana's rule book is short:

listitem.para: the company prefix is KXU followed by the five-digit company number, eight characters;
after the prefix comes the company's own reference, in upper-case letters and digits only, without hyphens or spaces;
no identifier is longer than 20 characters, which ISO/IEC 15459 recommends for a one-line bar code;

Codana adds no check character, as ISO/IEC 15459 itself adds none; the build checks instead that the prefix of every identifier is the company number of the party that issued it. A company may end its own reference with a check character if that makes its processes more robust, as Castrano does on its licence plates; it chooses the method (ISO/IEC 7064 gives systems for digits and for letters and digits, such as MOD 97-10 and MOD 37,2), and the character stays inside its own part of the number;
Codana does not hand out item numbers. It gives a company its number, and the company numbers its own items, lots, pallets and places.

section.para: What each thing looks like, for Valdara Industries, company number 10014:

The company's own reference in the globally unique form is its item number without its initials and hyphens: the mine's SM-ORE-L is KXU10252OREL, the packaging maker's RP-SF-23 is KXU15128SF23. In a document the company prefix KXU10014 is the scope within which the company gives its numbers.

The data identifier that a bar code puts in front of such a value (25P for an item, J for a transport unit) is not part of the value in a UBL document, where the element says what the value is. In a document the company's own number stays where it is (the seller's item identification, the serial, the lot); the globally unique form is the standard identification, given where a document crosses company borders and the receiver needs it. Which documents carry serials, lots, sites and returnable items in this form is not yet settled; none is numbered without a case.

The two systems meet in the park bench. Valdara ships it under its Codana form; Lumeway, as an importer may, gives it a GTIN from its own GS1 prefix for the shops, as its own number, and carries the maker's number alongside; where a document names the GTIN's issuer, it is Lumeway, not Codana. A reseller gives no GTIN of its own to an item that already has one: the store sells the mill's shirts under the mill's GTIN. A pallet needs no relabelling on the way: GS1 is itself an ISO/IEC 15459 issuing agency, so Lumeway's warehouse reads Castrano's licence plates and its own SSCCs alike. The engineering company, the sawmill, the island's cotton farm and ginnery and the utilities use only their own numbers. A reseller shows its own item number and the maker's. Inner packages have local numbers without a scheme. A logistic unit has the same identifier in every document of its flow, which the build checks.

section.title: Parties
section.para: The parties are the organisations of the world, chosen so that every party role in every UBL document type can be filled (see the party cover analysis). Each party has:

listitem.para: a role, such as manufacturer, road carrier or contracting authority;
a place on the map, in a town or a locality;

an identity: a name, the identifiers of its country's schemes, a postal address in its country's format, an electronic address, a main contact and the desks it works through (sales, purchasing, accounts receivable and payable, goods-in, dispatch, transport planning, customs, bids; a customs service has its export, import and transit offices, a chamber its certificates and carnet offices), and, where it is paid, an account at one of the world's banks. The role a party plays in a document picks the desk that speaks for it: the buyer's purchasing in an order, its accounts payable in an invoice, its goods-in in a receipt. The desks share the party's switchboard number; a small party such as the cotton farm has one office for everything;

for a company, its founding date, headcount and turnover, from which its size class follows by the Trade Accord's limits, modelled on the EU definition of small and medium-sized enterprises and given in all three currencies.

section.para: Names are invented and checked against real organisations. E-mail addresses use the reserved domain .example (RFC 2606), so that none can reach a real organisation. Telephone numbers use +999, which the ITU reserves for a future global service (ITU-T E.164), followed by the country's digit. Each country has its own numbering plan: Urvania kept the open plan of Italian times, with area codes of different lengths (9 or 10 digits); Bayvarra has a British-style plan of always 10 digits; the island has short 7-digit numbers. A telephone number has no relation to any identifier of its party. Account numbers follow the structure of ISO 13616 with its check digits, using the world's country codes, but they are not called IBANs, because the world's countries are not registered IBAN countries. Each country writes the bank and the branch into the account number in its own way: Bayvarra the bank code and a British-style six-digit sort code, Urvania the Italian-style ABI and CAB codes, the island the bank code and a three-digit branch number. A bank is identified across the countries by a code in the structure of ISO 9362, the BIC, with the world's country codes (BLUMXBLX), which the Trade Accord's payment link gives out, and its branch by the national code; the build checks that every account number holds the codes of its bank and branch.

An address has a number in its country's address register where it is a party's postal address or a delivery address: in Urvania one national register, like the Dutch one, sixteen digits starting with the code of the municipality; in Bayvarra a register per state, except in Lumeport, which keeps the city's own register (LUM-ADR-000417); on the island the post office's numbers of its delivery points, as the island has no postal codes. The build checks that the register is the one of the address's state or city.
Lisavu's farm register renews a grower's registration each season, so a farm's register entry carries an expiry date.

section.title: What a document says about a party
section.para: Master data is not copied from one record into every document. Each party is the authority on its own data, and every document stands on its own: no party relies on the other having kept an older document.

listitem.para: The sender describes itself in full for the kind of document. In a trade, payment or transport document, that means its identifiers, name, language, address, contact and electronic address. An invoice adds the sender's tax registration and legal entity. A customs or cross-border transport document adds the customs trader number. A tender, a catalogue or a business presentation adds what presents the company: its legal details, website and industry class.

The receiver is described with what the sender knows and needs. This may be less than the receiver says about itself, and never contradicts it. A buyer's order names the seller by number, name, address and electronic address. The seller's language comes in its order response, and its legal entity in its invoice. The answer completes the picture.
A third party (a carrier in a despatch advice, a bank, a party collected for) gets what the receiver needs to recognise or reach it.

section.para: The table per kind of document is analysis/party-profile.md, and the build checks it.

Company documents. Urvania's company law asks every company to state its register, its number in it, its legal form and its registered office on its invoices and business letters. An SUA also states its share capital as paid up, as the last balance sheet shows it, as Italian law asks of companies limited by shares (art. 2250 codice civile). Bayvarra and Lisavu follow the EU company-law directive (2017/1132, Art. 26), under which stating the capital is optional, and their companies leave it out. So only an Urvanian SUA's own invoices carry its share capital.

section.title: Items
section.para: Every party that sells has items. Goods carry what the documents along their way need: a seller's item identifier, a standard item identification where the party's identification system gives one (see "Two identification systems"), its classification in the UN Central Product Classification (CPC), its Harmonized System subheading and, in Urvania, the national tariff code below it, the country of origin, dimensions, net and gross weight, and the packaging. Services have a unit and a price. Units of measure and packaging types are UN/ECE Recommendation 20 and 21 codes from the UBL default code lists. Prices are in the seller's currency. A unit price may be finer than the currency, as an electricity tariff of 27.3 ferra per kilowatt hour is, but every amount to pay is rounded to the currency's minor unit.

Items connect the chains. The park bench is made with slats from the sawmill and film from the packaging maker; the distributor resells the bench, and its own item points to the manufacturer's, so the maker's identifiers travel along. A component or a resold item is only possible if the maker or reseller orders it from that seller somewhere in the flows.

An item's facts come in three layers, each known at a different moment. The item type and its variants are known when the product is designed: dimensions, materials, the standard colours, the warranty, the carbon footprint, the commodity code. The lot or the single piece is known when it is made, graded or tested: a production lot and its manufacture date, a casting's serial and melt number, the classing grade and moisture of a cotton lot. The transaction is known when the goods are ordered, shipped, measured or cleared: the variant chosen, anything made to order, the quantity and the price, the actual gross weight of a shipment, a seal number, a meter reading, the customs value. Two rules follow:

listitem.para: A fact is stated first in the document of the moment it becomes known: the type in the catalogue or the product information, the lot or piece in the document that accompanies the goods (a despatch advice, a certificate, a weight statement), the transaction in its own document (the order, the despatch advice, the invoice, the declaration).
A later document repeats a fact only if its own transaction uses it. Otherwise it identifies the item, the lot or the earlier document, and the reader finds the fact there.

section.para: The rules work in both directions: a catalogue with a lot number is as wrong as an invoice with the search keywords. Companies keep their item data in step through catalogues, and every later document points to the item by its identifier. A reader who follows one bench through its documents sees it gain facts: a type in the catalogue, a variant in the order, a lot and serial numbers when it leaves the factory, a weight and a seal on the truck, a value at the border. A catalogue line adds the seller's terms (lead time, minimum and maximum quantity, the price list and its validity); a despatch advice names the production lot, or the serial number of every casting, which stays the same when a cancelled despatch advice is replaced; and a till receipt during a promotion shows the discount on the shelf price. What each kind of document carries is fixed in the item table (analysis/item-profile.md): a catalogue or an offer everything about the type; an order the identification and the variant chosen; a despatch advice the lots, serials and dangerous goods; an invoice the identification and what tax needs; a customs declaration the description, commodity code and origin; a shopper's receipt the name, the brand and the warranty.

The colours an item comes in are facts of its type, listed in the catalogue as variants; an order names the variant it wants by its identifier and states nothing new about the item. Only a colour the catalogue does not offer is specified in the order, as something made to order. Where the shopper sees and chooses the variant, as the wood of the Marrow bench and chair, each variant is a trade item of its own with a GTIN of its own, as GS1 asks: the maker keeps one item number for the model and adds the variant to it, and the store gives each variant a number of its own. A product's carbon footprint is stated per lifecycle stage, the supply of raw materials and the making of the product, as two figures that add up to the total.
Items are combined in four ways, each shown by a case the world already has:

listitem.para: A single item, ordered and sold alone, with its own number: the Elderwick Marrow bench in oak, or the chair in ash.
A pack of the same item, n times the same packed as one unit: the sawmill's bundle of 50 hardwood bench slats. The item and the pack are two levels, each with its own number.

A kit of different items, wrapped in one package and sold as one: the Elderwick care kit for the Marrow dining furniture (a 250 ml tin of hard-wax oil and a lint-free cloth), or the ground anchor set of the park bench. A kit is one item with its own number and a stated content; on the GS1 side it has a GTIN of its own, because it is physically combined.

An offer, items bought together for less but never one package: the Marrow set of a bench and two chairs in one wood, 899 lume in the shop instead of 947. It has no number of its own; each piece keeps its own, and a document that shows the sale carries a line per piece and a "Marrow set" allowance. GS1 calls this a virtual bundle and treats it as a selling arrangement, not a trade item.

section.para: The content of the slat bundle and the anchor set is settled with their flows; the care kit's is given above. A cotton bale is not a pack: its nominal weight of about 227 kg belongs to the item's description, the number of bales to the shipment, and each bale's real weight to the weight statement.

Brands. Elderwick is Brightmarket Stores' own label for home and garden, built to stand as a brand of its own, as most retailers' private labels are. The Elderwick Marrow bench (1400 mm) and the Elderwick Marrow chair are dining furniture for indoors, in solid kiln-dried oak or ash with a hard-wax oil finish, a closed seat, glued joints, felt pads under the legs and a seat height of about 45 cm. Each comes in oak and in ash, and the shopper chooses; the store plans three oak pieces for every two in ash. Brackenmere Furniture makes them to the store's specification and sells them to the store at 380 and 115 lume, the same in both woods; the store sells them in its home and garden department at 549 and 199, from the day the department reopens after its renovation, Monday 11 May, and gives a care kit free with each bench. The stock comes in March and waits for the reopening; the line is taken on sale-or-return terms for its first four weeks of sales; at the end of the trial the stock above the target goes back to Brackenmere in the store's van, at Brackenmere's cost: Brackenmere credits it in full, and the store invoices the transport. The store asked for seat pads as an option; Brackenmere quoted a pad of its own brand for the chair, made for it by a textile workshop, and the store did not take it, because it sells seat pads from its own textile range. Many shoppers buy the chairs alone, because the 1400 mm bench is too long for many apartment kitchens. The shopper sees the store's label, and the maker's name is on no label: Elderwick is the world's case of an item whose brand owner and manufacturer are different parties. The shirts the store sells are the other way round: they carry the textile mill's own brand, Lumeport, so the mill numbers them from its own GS1 prefix. Under GS1's rules the brand owner numbers the item, so the bench and the chair in each wood and the care kit each have a GTIN from Brightmarket's prefix, whoever sells them: five GTINs; the set, being an offer, has none. Brackenmere sells its own office and outdoor furniture under its own name: the office desk, the park bench PB-2 it tenders with, and the furnishing of public offices with installation.

section.title: The park bench
section.para: The park bench Serra 180 is the item the world follows furthest. It is made of two side frames of ductile cast iron (EN-GJS-400-15), galvanised and powder-coated, of 11.1 kg each; five slats of thermally modified ash of 1,800 × 95 × 45 mm at 4.24 kg each, which the sawmill in Marrowdale modifies in a kiln of its own and which are left untreated to turn silver-grey; and a set of 20 stainless A4 bolts with nuts and washers: 44.1 kg in all. It is 1,800 mm long over the slats and 1,660 mm over the armrests. It is bolted to the ground with four anchors, which are a separate item. A spare side frame is classified as a part of a seat (HS 9401.99), because it is made for the bench; the anchors and bolts are parts of general use and stay in the metal chapters. The bench's figures come from a parametric model of it, with drawings, in world/bench/.

The bench ships knocked down, in three parcels that a person can carry: two frame cartons of 790 × 680 × 100 mm, of 12.2 kg and 13.0 kg (the second with the bolts), and a strapped bundle of five slats of 21.8 kg, 1.81 m long, which two people carry because of its length: 47.0 kg gross. A spare side frame is simply one frame carton. Four benches make a pallet of 1,850 × 700 × 745 mm and about 216 kg, with the pallet's own 28.2 kg, moved by fork-lift and stacked two high; 24 such pallets and a pallet of frame cartons take 13 floor positions of a 13.6 m trailer or a 40-foot container. An installation crew of two assembles and anchors the benches in a park; a shopper who buys one has the three parcels delivered.

The three countries apply the limit of ISO 11228-1 for manual handling: 25 kg for one person in good conditions, and about two thirds of the combined capacity for two people lifting together. Goods are packed so that a parcel a person lifts stays within it. Anything heavier is moved by machine, as a pallet is by fork-lift and a cotton bale of about 227 kg is, and the documents say so.

The bench's goods chain runs through the documents of several flows. Valdara makes to order, in lots: a lot has a date, a quantity and a coating batch, every side frame has a serial number that rises with the day it was cast, and every casting day has its own melt number. Lumeway holds stock in Marrowdale. It receives 96 benches and 12 spare frames by road on 25 March and 192 benches by rail on 15 April, and sells from that stock in the order the goods arrived: 24 benches to Brightmarket on 29 April, and 104 benches and the 12 frames to Velumi on the island on 13 May. The store refuses one of its 24 benches at goods-in, damaged; it goes back to Marrowdale on the truck the same day and is held apart as damaged stock, not for sale. At the end of May Lumeway holds 161 benches, 160 for sale and the damaged one. Velumi buys by the pallet: of its 104 benches, on 26 pallets of four, 96 are for the Port of Selanu's harbour parks and two pallets are for its own stock, from which its shop sells two benches to a cotton farm in June; six remain. An urgent order does not come from stock: when Velumi asks for eight more frames on 11 May, Lumeway has none, so Valdara casts them and they pass through Lumeway's dispatch area to the aircraft, a cross-dock. They are spares for the port's harbour benches and travel under the Accord's common transit from Ferrano to Selanu airport. Booked on the afternoon flight of 13 May, they reach the cargo terminal after the cut-off, because the truck from Ferrano is late, and fly the next morning; Lumeway cancels its despatch advice, which named the missed flight, and replaces it. Valdara also sells direct: 40 benches to the public works department on 30 March, from a lot of their own, and two benches travel to a fair under a carnet.

section.title: Billing
section.para: An invoice requests payment. A supplier may invoice on despatch, as Valdara Industries does, or after the customer's receipt advice. A credit note is the supplier's document for what the customer does not owe after all. A debit note is its counterpart: the supplier's addition to an invoice it issued, when more is due than was charged; it refers to that invoice and gives the reason. It is not a buyer's claim against its supplier. When a buyer has a claim on its supplier (a service the buyer performed, a cost it had to bear, a contract penalty), the world uses an invoice from the buyer, a credit note from the supplier, or a deduction shown in the remittance advice, as the flow's story requires.

The world's debit notes come from the rail delivery to Lumeway. Its framework contract gives a container five free days at the consignee's siding, counted from the day after it is placed, and then charges 7,500 ferra per container day. The second container waits two days beyond that, because Lumeway's fork-lift is in repair: the freight invoice was right when it was issued, and more became due afterwards by a rule of the contract. So Ferrano Rail Cargo adds the demurrage to its freight invoice with a debit note to Valdara, the transport user, and Valdara, whose buyer bears a delay in unloading under DAP, adds it to its goods invoice with a debit note to Lumeway. A bonus that is known before the invoice, such as the ore train's for arriving on the first day of its window, is a charge on the invoice.

section.title: Tax and customs
section.para: A seller states its own country's tax. An Urvanian seller's invoice shows Urvanian value added tax or the reason none is due; a Bayvarran seller's shows the state sales tax or an exemption; a Lisavan seller's has no tax section at all: no tax total, no tax category on the line and no tax scheme. Nothing is implied by that absence, because the totals state it: the amount without tax, the amount with tax and the amount to pay are equal. Taxes the island does have keep their section. Urvania does not tax a service supplied outside Urvania, to a customer established abroad or on land abroad; it exempts the carriage of goods directly linked to their export, as most VAT systems do, so the barge operator's freight for the granulate going down the river to Bayvarra carries no Urvanian tax and says why; and Urvania also levies an energy tax per kilowatt hour, in two tiers, on which value added tax is then charged.

Bayvarra taxes what foreign businesses earn from its public purse, at source. A public body in Bayvarra withholds 10 % of the price of a service from a business not established there and pays it to the state; such a supplier names a tax representative in Bayvarra, registered with the tax office. It is a tax on income, not a sales tax, and it applies to public bodies only: a company withholds nothing from a foreign carrier. On the island, a buyer of farm produce withholds a presumptive tax, 1 % of a delivery's value up to 2,000 coral and 2 % above, and the farm collects a levy of 1 % for the cotton fund of the chamber of commerce; seed cotton is priced from the trade accord's lint reference price, published in lume. Lumeport's water company also collects the city's sewage levy, as a line collected on behalf of the city, and runs the city's district heating.

Bayvarra's retail sales tax falls on the final use, so what a business buys is exempt only where it does not end there. What a business sells on as it is, or what becomes part of the product it sells (raw materials, ingredients, components, the packaging that goes to the customer), is a sale for resale or manufacture and exempt; what it uses up or keeps (fuel and energy it burns, consumables, tools, machines, vehicles, buildings) is taxed as a retail sale; services to a business are exempt. A waste plant paid a gate fee sells a disposal service, exempt to a business and taxed to a household; a plant that buys waste as fuel buys taxable goods. So the propane the water company burns in its boilers carries the sales tax of Coastal State, where it is delivered, and the district heat it sells a household carries it again, as in Washington or California, whose sales taxes exempt an ingredient or component and tax fuel used to make heat. Unlike Urvania's value added tax, which taxes every purchase and lets the business deduct it, a retail sales tax keeps the tax a business pays on its inputs.

Goods of Accord origin cross the borders free of duty, on proof of origin: every import declaration claims the preference, names the criterion (wholly obtained, sufficiently processed, or regional value content) and refers to its proof of origin. The proof is a certificate of origin from a chamber of commerce where the exporter asks for one, or else the exporter's statement on origin on its commercial invoice, worded as the origin declarations of the EU's preferential arrangements. Each country names the bodies that may issue the certificates under the Accord; Urvania has authorised its chambers of commerce, as real agreements delegate this to chambers too. The exporter applies with a document of its own; the chamber checks it, issues the certificate under its own number and is its only endorser, for a certificate between Accord members needs no legalisation by an embassy. Goods from outside the Accord pay each country's own tariff. What is still due at the border differs. In Urvania, value added tax of 20 % on the value with freight to the border, which a business deducts again. In Bayvarra nothing, because its sales tax is charged once, at the final retail sale. In Lisavu the import consumption tax of 10 % on the landed value, whatever the goods' origin, so imported goods cost more on the island than on the mainland: freight, and 10 % on top.

Medicines are the exception on both counts. Bayvarra's and Lisavu's tariffs charge no duty on medicines (HS chapter 30) nor on radioactive isotopes for medicine (HS 2844.43), whatever their origin, as most countries do, many under the WTO's zero-for-zero agreement on pharmaceutical products. And Lisavu exempts from its import consumption tax the medicines and vaccines supplied to a public hospital, and their import for that supply: one exemption reason in its national list (MEDHOSP); the rule of 10 % on every import stays for everything else. Its real parallel is Sweden's VAT law, Mervärdesskattelag (2023:200) chapter 10 § 13, which exempts deliveries of medicines to hospitals and their import with such a delivery.

The world also trades beyond the Accord. The medicines of the island's hospital come from two makers abroad, invented companies in real countries: an isotope maker in the Netherlands, which invoices in euro, and a vaccine maker in Hyderabad, India, which invoices in rupees and asks to be paid in euro. Their goods fly to Lumeport by scheduled air cargo of carriers the documents do not name, and the wholesaler that buys them imports them into Bayvarra. These makers have no place on the map and no identifier of a real register in the documents, since a number in the real format could be someone's: they are named by their name and address. Their invoices and the wholesaler's customs values use the rates of the day: the ECB's for the rupee against the euro, the Lumeport Exchange's fixing for the lume.

Goods may also cross a land border under the Accord's common transit procedure, modelled on the convention on a common transit procedure of 20 May 1987, which the EEC and the EFTA countries concluded and which today joins the European Union and eleven other common transit countries. The holder of the procedure lodges one transit declaration at the office of departure; the goods travel under seal past the offices of exit and of transit, and the procedure ends at the office of destination, where the importer declares them for import, citing the transit declaration as the previous one. The declaration's jurisdiction is the Accord, not the country of departure alone. Valdara's containers by rail travel so, from the customs office at the Ferrano hub to Bayvarra customs' inland office at Marrowdale.

Valuation is national too, within the WTO's rules on customs valuation. In all three countries the value starts from the price actually paid, and charges that are part of that price (a special finish, export packing) belong to it. Urvania includes freight and insurance to its border, in the continental way. Bayvarra values goods as they left the exporting country, without freight and insurance, in the settlers' tradition, as the United States, Canada and Australia do.
